transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10
Time: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees:
  - Elena Park (Redwood, AE)
  - Devon Singh (Redwood, SE)
  - Priya Rao (Redwood, CSM)
  - Raj Patel (Nimble Finance, Head of Platform)
  - Sofia Morales (Nimble Finance, ML Eng)
  - Liam O'Brien (Nimble Finance, Security)
  - Hannah Kim (Nimble Finance, DevOps)

Quick summary (auto):
  - Onboarding is ~60% complete; primary blockers are KMS/HSM access, VPC peering rules, and a failing SAML assertion in test environment.
  - SE to run a targeted latency bench with KV cache and sample traffic shape; customer to provide subnet/egress details and open KMS ticket.

Topics:
  - Access and credentialing status
  - KMS/HSM onboarding path and encryption concerns
  - VPC peering, egress, and firewall rules for Redwood Private
  - Latency benchmark design and KV cache behavior
  - Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Elena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We're gonna try to keep this tight — 45 minutes. Quick roll-call and then status.
[00:06] Raj Patel: Yep, Raj here. Quick note, we're on sick day rotation but I'll own platform side.
[00:10] Sofia Morales: Sofia, ML. We ran the initial eval, saw token cost estimates, a couple of weird outliers in latency.
[00:15] Liam O'Brien: Liam, security — I have notes on KMS and audit logs.
[00:18] Devon Singh: Devon (Redwood SE) — I'll go through the bench plan and KV cache questions.
[00:22] Elena Park: Ok, Priya you're with CSM; want to call out anything?
[00:26] Priya Rao: Just tracking the onboarding checklist, we'll flag when gate is clear.

[00:35] Elena Park: High level: onboarding progress - we see your account in our staging cluster, tokens issued, service account created, but the SAML assertion failed on first login and KMS key grant isn't complete. Hannah, you had a note?
[00:45] Hannah Kim: Yeah, we tried the SAML flow using our IdP test connector — the nameID mapping was off, the assertion says email but IdP provides uid. we can change it but wanted to confirm Redwood's required attribute map.
[00:55] Elena Park: Cool, I will share the SSO mapping doc after. Quick note — sometimes the attribute is labeled 'mail' and the IdP uses 'mail' vs 'email', that trips the auto-mapper.
[01:05] Raj Patel: Good to know. On KMS — we need assurance for keys staying in our HSM and that logs are auditable. Does Redwood support BYOK where keys never leave our HSM?
[01:15] Devon Singh: Short answer: yes, for Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM via a proxy. Keys never persist in our control plane. We do store key reference ids and rotate ephemeral session tokens. There's a small caveat around dedicated backups — but we can walk through that in the security doc.
[01:28] Liam O'Brien: And you have audit logs for every encryption operation? Need them to ship to our SIEM.
[01:34] Devon Singh: Yes — we can stream audit events to your SIEM, and we have pluggable hooks. We will send a sample events schema.

[01:50] Sofia Morales: On the performance side: earlier bench runs had a long tail at 99th percentile when sequence length increased. We suspect KV cache miss rate was high in staging. Is there a way to instrument cache hit ratios?
[02:02] Devon Singh: Absolutely — our runtime exposes per-model cache hit/miss metrics and per-route token breakdowns in the Consolee — sorry "Console" — we call it out as latency breakdowns and per-route traces. We can enable debug-level cache metrics for your staging tests.
[02:15] Sofia Morales: Great. Also, can we control batching — we need low latency for interactive flows, so we'd prefer small batch sizes. But we want to understand token cost tradeoffs.
[02:25] Devon Singh: You can control batching via route config: max batch size and max wait. For interactive low-latency we suggest small max batch (1-4) and aggressive timeout; leverage KV cache to reduce cost. We can run a comparison run: batch=1 vs batch=8 and show cost/latency.

[02:48] Hannah Kim: On network: VPC peering and egress rules — our infra team needs the exact outbound IP list or we do peering? What's Redwood's pattern for Private?
[02:58] Elena Park: For Redwood Private we support both VPC peering and allowlist egress IPs. For the initial POC many customers do forced egress allowlist. I'll attach the egress ranges and recommended ports. If you want peering, we have a peering playbook but it takes a bit longer due to routing.
[03:15] Hannah Kim: Ok, peering will be a follow-up; for now we'll open firewall rules and do allowlist. We need the precise CIDRs.
[03:22] Elena Park: Will send them today.

[03:28] Raj Patel: About telemetry — we want token-level cost but also per-customer attribution. Is that available?
[03:33] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood Console offers token-level billing per API key and per-route. We can provide a sample billing export.

[03:40] Sofia Morales: For the benchmark run, Sophie (sic) sorry — Sofia, we'd like the SE to simulate production traffic with mixed prompt lengths, several concurrency levels, and a KV cache enabling. What specific config do you need?
[03:52] Devon Singh: We need a traffic profile (percent short/medium/long), concurrency target, target qps, model variant, and whether to enable cache priming. Send that as a spreadsheet and we'll template the run. Also we recommend a warm-up phase to populate KV.
[04:05] Sofia Morales: We have a small dataset of 2k sample prompts; we'll share distribution + desired qps (250).

[04:12] Liam O'Brien: One more on compliance — do you support fixed retention windows and can we disable conversation retention entirely?
[04:18] Devon Singh: For Private you control data retention; you can set retention to 0 and disable logs at route-level. We will enumerate all logs in the doc. For hosted we have retention controls but audit requirements differ.

[04:30] Elena Park: Ok let's summarize blockers: 1) SAML attribute mapping — quick fix; 2) KMS/HSM key grant and ticket; 3) firewall/egress CIDRs for allowlist; 4) design of the latency bench + KV cache instrumentation.

[04:40] Raj Patel: Anything else on cost? Our CFO wants a rough monthly unit cost for the expected traffic. Sofia you had estimates?
[04:47] Sofia Morales: Based on the pilot shape we're seeing token costs in the sim; can you confirm Redwood's quantization options? We wanted to explore int8 vs int4 to reduce token CPU cost.
[04:58] Devon Singh: We have quantized runtimes and quant recommendations per model. For some models int4 is supported and provides lower memory and cost tradeoffs; we'll share quantization profiles and a suggested quality test to ensure no regression.

[05:12] Hannah Kim: A small practical ask — can you provide a minimal iptables example for egress rules to our dev cluster so we can test quickly?
[05:20] Elena Park: Yes — I'll include a short iptables snippet and a Terraform snippet for allowlist.

[05:28] Priya Rao: I'll track owners: we're marking this week as partial gate. Once KMS and SAML are resolved we can move to "staging clear".

[05:38] Devon Singh: For the bench run we propose: 1) warm up phase with 5k priming requests, 2) 10k steady-state requests at 250 qps with 70% short/20% med/10% long prompt distribution, 3) capture cache hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies and token cost.
[05:57] Sofia Morales: Sounds good. Would you also run a second run with batching=1 and batching=8?
[06:03] Devon Singh: Yep, we'll do both and annotate the tradeoffs.

[06:12] Elena Park: Any competing solutions in play or parallel evals?
[06:15] Raj Patel: We're also talking to Vertex AI and a small on-prem team evaluating a custom runtime.
[06:20] Elena Park: Noted.

[06:24] Liam O'Brien: Last question — can Redwood rotate keys on demand and provide retention proof to auditors?
[06:29] Devon Singh: Yes, key rotation via your KMS policy is supported; we can also generate signed proof-of-rotation events for auditors.

[06:38] Elena Park: Ok, wrap. Recap next steps and owners: I'll send SSO mapping + egress CIDRs + iptables/Terraform snippets. Devon will schedule bench and send template for traffic profile. Hannah will open KMS ticket and share subnets. Priya will update the gating status in the tracker.

[06:54] Raj Patel: Good meeting, thanks.
[06:56] Sofia Morales: Thanks everyone.
[06:57] Elena Park: Thanks, will follow up with the docs and calendar for the bench.

Auto end notes:
- Links referenced: SSO mapping doc (to be shared), Security summary (SOC2), Bench template spreadsheet (link to be provided).
